chunks: From him, from one of his companions, raising it (the hadith), said:

The one who says after every prayer, while holding his beard with his right hand, 'O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, have mercy on me from the Fire,' three times, with his left hand raised, its palm facing the sky. Then he says, 'Rescue me from the painful punishment,' three times.

Then he lowers his hand from his beard, then raises his hand and makes its palm facing the sky, then says, 'O Mighty, O Generous, O Beneficent, O Merciful,' and flips his hands, making both their palms facing the sky, then says, 'Rescue me from the painful punishment,' three times.

Send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and the Angels, and the Spirit. Forgiveness is granted to him, and he is pleased, and forgiveness is linked to him until all creatures die, except for the two heavy ones, the Jinn and humans.
And he said: When you have finished your Tashahhud, raise your hands and say:

O Allah, forgive me with a decisive and firm forgiveness that leaves no sin, and I do not commit a prohibition after it ever. Grant me well-being with no affliction after it ever. Guide me with guidance after which I do not go astray ever. Benefit me, O Lord, with what You taught me, make it for me, and not against me. Provide me with sufficiency and make me content with it.

O Lord! Turn to me. O Allah, O Allah, O Allah. O Beneficent, O Beneficent, O Beneficent. O Merciful, O Merciful, O Merciful. Have mercy on me from the Fire of blazing heat. Extend upon me from the abundance of Your provision. Guide me to what differed regarding the Truth by Your permission. Protect me from the Pelted Satan. Convey to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) from me many greetings and peace. Guide me by Your guidance. Enrich me with Your richness. Make me from Your sincere friends. And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad. Ameen.
He said: The one who says this after every prayer, Allah will return his soul to him in his grave, and he will be alive, sustained, blissful, and joyful until the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting the specific post-prayer supplication mentioned in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this supplication from *Al-Kafi* emphasizes the integration of physical humility—such as holding the beard and raising palms—with profound verbal invocation, reflecting the concept of *tawassul* through divine attributes like *Al-Aziz* and *Al-Karim*. The promise of spiritual vitality in the grave (*barzakh*) underscores the continuity of worship beyond the ritual, linking immediate post-prayer devotion to eternal reward and protection from the Fire.
